judged_text: The members endpoint applies no bounds on the client-supplied limit/offset, accepting arbitrary values such as limit=1000000 or negative offset. A client (the new pagination UI or any API consumer) can request an unbounded member serialization, turning the new pagination feature into a full-table dump and defeating the page-size invariant the change was supposed to enforce.

record.issue_text: [ADVISORY] The members endpoint applies no bounds on the client-supplied limit/offset, accepting arbitrary values such as limit=1000000 or negative offset. A client (the new pagination UI or any API consumer) can request an unbounded member serialization, turning the new pagination feature into a full-table dump and defeating the page-size invariant the change was supposed to enforce.

adjudication.rationale: In `GroupsController#members`, the new pagination params are taken directly from the request with no clamping/validation: `limit = (params[:limit] || 50).to_i` and `offset = params[:offset].to_i`, then used in `group.users...limit(limit).offset(offset)`. This allows arbitrarily large `limit` (e.g., 1000000) to force serialization of essentially the full member list, and potentially negative/invalid values as well. The client-side `Group#findMembers` clamps offset, but the server endpoint remains unbounded for any API consumer, so the finding is verifiable from the diff.
